title: Ejector Ending
textLines: You rush to the bridge controls, eyes scanning the glowing panels as alarms scream through the ship.
Your fingers fly over the interface until a schematic of the Cargo Hold flashes onto the screen—a bright red dot pulsing in one corner,
marking the location of the containment breach.
The red glare of the bridge's emergency lights merges with the warning indicators, painting everything in a sickly crimson haze.
The back corner of the bay is completely blown out.
If you don't seal it and eject the cargo, the breach could tear the ship apart.
You pull up the life-support diagnostics.
One faint blip shows up on the scanner—a single life sign in the Cargo Hold. It's not moving.
A timer flashes beside it:
Life Support Failure in: 00:35
Whoever's down there has less than a minute before the vacuum takes them.
They're probably already unconscious.
You take a steadying breath and tell yourself that's a comfort.
Your hand hovers for a moment over the Eject Cargo command.
Then you press it.
A low rumble vibrates through the hull. The bridge shudders as the cargo clamps release and the hold detaches.
Through the viewport, you watch crates, debris, and twisted metal drift slowly away—spinning toward the black hole's horizon.
Then, among the tumbling wreckage, something catches your eye.
A figure.
A person in a space suit, drifting with the cargo.
The suit flashes briefly as it turns, catching the ship's lights before fading into the blackness beyond.
A hollow weight settles in your stomach.
Whoever they were, they'd made it into a suit—maybe even stood a chance.
Probably not.
But you can't shake the feeling that there might have been another way.
You stand there for a long moment, watching until the last fragments vanish into the dark.
What's done is done.
Now, it's time to find out what's really happening on this ship.
